input.question: Which award did Philip Proctor receive?

documents.text:
Title: The Industrialist's Honor: Philip Proctor's Rise to Knighthood

In the early 20th century, New Zealand was undergoing a period of rapid industrialization, and at the forefront of this transformation was Philip Proctor, a visionary entrepreneur who would leave an indelible mark on the nation's economy. Born and raised in Auckland, Proctor's innate business acumen and innovative spirit drove him to establish a series of successful ventures, cementing his reputation as a leading industrialist of his time. As Proctor's empire expanded, so did his influence. He became a respected voice in the business community, known for his progressive ideas and commitment to social welfare. His dedication to the betterment of New Zealand's industrial landscape did not go unnoticed, and in 1923, he was recognized for his outstanding contributions with the prestigious award of Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire. This esteemed honor, conferred upon Proctor by King George V, was a testament to his tireless efforts in promoting the growth and development of New Zealand's industries. The Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire, a rank within the Order of the British Empire, is one of the highest honors bestowed upon individuals for their exceptional service to the Commonwealth. Proctor's remarkable journey to knighthood was paved by his pioneering work in the manufacturing sector. In the early 1900s, he founded the Proctor Manufacturing Company, which quickly became a leading producer of textiles, machinery, and other essential goods. His innovative approach to production, which emphasized efficiency, quality, and worker welfare, set a new standard for industrial practices in New Zealand. As his business empire expanded, Proctor's philanthropic efforts also gained momentum. He was a vocal advocate for workers' rights, and his companies were known for providing fair wages, safe working conditions, and opportunities for social mobility. His commitment to the well-being of his employees earned him widespread respect and admiration, both within the business community and among the general public. Proctor's contributions to New Zealand's war effort during World War I further solidified his reputation as a dedicated patriot. He played a crucial role in mobilizing the nation's industrial resources, ensuring a steady supply of essential goods and materials to the Allied forces. His selfless dedication to the war effort did not go unnoticed, and in 1918, he was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire, a precursor to his eventual knighthood.

accepted_answers: Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire
